policy.purpose: Difficulty- and prior-knowledge-aware SBA teaching map between Core1 and Core2.
policy.primary_question_rule: Each Q01-Q59 has exactly one primary SBA bucket.
policy.production_selection_rule: Skip dedicated SBA PDFs when primary question count is zero.
policy.priority_rule: Prioritise D2-D4 buckets for learners at or below 50% usable prior knowledge.
policy.core2_hint_preteach_rule: Every Core2 H1/H2/H3 reveal must trace to earlier Core1A teaching; release prerequisites may delay a question.
policy.teaching_sequence_rule: Pretrain -> visual stages -> physics meaning -> maths -> worked/guided practice -> retrieval -> Core2.

required_support_20pct: full rebuild+staged visual+derivation+multiple examples+guided transfer+hint audit

buckets.production_reason: Primary Core2 present; source-visible extension requires a full 20-percent learner bridge without inventing missing source theory.

learning_atoms.title: Slope as a line
learning_atoms.purpose: Build the inclined landing surface in ordinary ground axes before any projectile algebra.
teaching_moves: draw +x and +y with an incline through the origin
misconceptions: an inclined landing surface can still be treated as y=0
checks: write the line equation for a plane through the launch point

learning_atoms.title: Projectile path in the same axes
learning_atoms.purpose: Place the projectile trajectory and the plane in one common coordinate frame.
teaching_moves: draw trajectory and plane from the same origin
label alpha from +x and beta for the plane
misconceptions: the launch angle should be measured from the incline rather than from the chosen +x axis without conversion
checks: identify alpha, beta and the two y-functions on one diagram

learning_atoms.title: Impact is the second intersection
learning_atoms.purpose: Translate landing on a slope into equality of two y-values at one non-zero x.
teaching_moves: show launch point as the first intersection
show the later impact as the second intersection
misconceptions: keep the launch root x=0 as the landing point
checks: state the correct impact equation before solving

learning_atoms.title: Find range on the inclined plane
learning_atoms.purpose: Derive horizontal impact coordinate first, then convert it to distance measured along the plane.
misconceptions: horizontal x is the same as range measured along the incline
checks: derive or reconstruct the four-step inclined-range method

learning_atoms.title: Horizontal projection versus along-plane distance
learning_atoms.purpose: Make x=s cos beta visually obvious so geometry does not get mixed with projectile dynamics.
teaching_moves: draw a right triangle from the impact point
misconceptions: AB equals its horizontal projection AC
checks: convert between x and s without using projectile equations

learning_atoms.title: Time-known inclined-plane geometry
learning_atoms.purpose: Use a stated time to obtain the horizontal projection, then use plane geometry for the requested inclined length.
teaching_moves: use x=u cos alpha times t
mark the impact point on the plane
misconceptions: a stated time means the trajectory equation must always be used
checks: solve a time-known projection problem in two steps

learning_atoms.title: Normal impact is a direction condition
learning_atoms.purpose: Teach that normal impact means perpendicular to the plane, not vertical.
teaching_moves: rotate the plane direction by 90 degrees
express impact direction as beta+90 degrees
misconceptions: normal to an incline means vertical
checks: state the impact-velocity direction for a given beta

learning_atoms.title: Translate normal direction into velocity components
learning_atoms.purpose: Connect the normal direction to v_y/v_x while keeping the ordinary projectile velocity equations.
misconceptions: a negative vertical component means negative speed
checks: write the velocity-ratio constraint for normal impact

learning_atoms.title: Two simultaneous impact constraints
learning_atoms.purpose: Combine point-on-plane and velocity-direction conditions using the same impact time.
misconceptions: satisfying the velocity direction alone guarantees the projectile is on the plane
checks: set up both normal-impact constraints before solving for alpha

hint_rungs.evidence: Impact on a slope is taught as the second intersection, not y=0.
Plane and trajectory are drawn and written as y-functions in the same ground axes.
Independent practice rehearses setting y_projectile=y_plane before solving the non-zero intersection.
A stated time is converted to horizontal displacement using u cos(alpha) times t.
The projection triangle distinguishes horizontal x from along-plane distance s.
Independent practice rehearses s=x/cos(beta) as the first geometry move after x is known.
Normal impact is explicitly taught as velocity perpendicular to the incline, direction beta+90 degrees.
The point-on-plane and impact-direction constraints are taught together as simultaneous event conditions.
Worked and independent practice first write v_x, v_y and impose the velocity ratio before eliminating impact time.
